annotation.title_clean: 文化适配性视角下社交机器人技术接受度研究——基于信任、语言与伦理的TLE模型构建
annotation.title_en: A Study of Social Robot Technology Acceptance from the Perspective of Cultural Suitability—Construction of a TLE Model Based on Trust, Language and Ethics
annotation.venue: Advances in Philosophy 哲学进展
named_instruments_referenced: UNESCO Recommendation on the Ethics of AI
annotation.summary_en: Conceptual paper proposing a TLE model (trust, language/communication, ethics) to explain cross-cultural acceptance of social robots, with a focus on China, Confucian ethics and elder care. It argues cultural adaptation of transparency, language and ethical values is needed, citing Chinese AI policies and the EU AI Act.
key_provisions_or_claims: Proposes TLE three-dimensional model mapped to DeLone & McLean system, information and service quality.
Cross-cultural technological trust must be calibrated with ethical values.
Language localisation must cover symbolic systems and cultural pragmatics (high- vs low-context).
Confucian 'ren' ethics offers a complement to Western privacy-centred AI ethics.
Recommends trustworthy AI certification and ethics-by-design for social robots in China.
